scripts.hint: Rayo follows a mysterious song to the lighthouse and guides a lost baby boat home.
lines: Rayo: Who is singing that soft song across the dark sea?
Rayo: Today I follow the singing sound along the coast road!
Rayo: Teddy, listen — the song gets louder near the pier!
Teddy: The fishing boats are bobbing like they dance to it, Rayo!
Rayo: I drive along the harbour wall, past the sleepy docked boats.
Teddy: Look, Rayo! A tiny lighthouse stands on the rocky point!
Rayo: The path climbs the cliff, twisty and narrow and steep.
Rayo: I beep twice at the seagulls sitting on the cliff fence.
Teddy: The singing is coming from the top of the lighthouse!
Rayo: Oh no! The lighthouse lamp is off — the tower is dark!
Rayo: Down below, a little baby boat is lost in the fog!
Teddy: Wait, Rayo... the song is the wind blowing through the tower pipes!
Rayo: The keeper is asleep — I must wake him with my loudest beep!
Rayo: Beep beep beep! Wake up, keeper! A boat needs your light!
Teddy: The keeper woke up, Rayo! He is climbing the tower stairs!
Rayo: The great lamp turns on, sweeping gold across the waves!
Teddy: The baby boat sees the light — she is turning towards home!
Rayo: I flash my headlights to cheer her all the way in.
Rayo: The baby boat is safe in the harbour, rocking gently.
Teddy: The keeper waves and gives us a shiny brass bell!
Rayo: We hang the bell on my mirror — ding ding, what a sound!
Rayo: The wind sings one last soft song through the pipes.
Teddy: Goodnight, lighthouse! Keep shining for every little boat.
Rayo: A brave car always helps friends find their way home.
Rayo: Tomorrow I will visit the apple orchard on the hill — will you come with me?
scripts.title: Rayo and the Singing Lighthouse

scripts.hint: Bella follows a trail of butterflies and finds a baby duck who needs her help.
lines: Bella: Why are a hundred butterflies flying in one long ribbon?
Bella: Today I follow the butterflies into the big garden!
Bella: Pip, sit on my roof — we are going through the garden gate!
Pip: The rose path smells sweeter than honey, Bella!
Bella: I roll slowly past the fountain where goldfish jump.
Pip: Look, Bella! The butterflies are circling the sunflower field!
Bella: My tall yellow roof almost touches the sunflower heads.
Bella: I cross the little wooden bridge over the lily pond.
Pip: A frog on a lily pad is croaking a welcome song!
Bella: Oh no! The butterfly ribbon suddenly stops at the hedge!
Bella: I hear a tiny peep-peep coming from the tall grass.
Pip: Wait, Bella... something small and fluffy is stuck in the grass!
Bella: It is a baby duck, all alone and calling for her mother!
Bella: Hop onto my warm bonnet, little duck — we will find her.
Pip: The butterflies are flying again — they know the way!
Bella: We follow them past the picnic lawn and the old oak tree.
Pip: There! The mother duck is swimming on the garden lake!
Bella: The baby duck slides down my door and splashes to her mother.
Pip: What a happy reunion — the whole pond is quacking!
Bella: The butterflies land on my roof like a living crown.
Bella: I drive home slowly through the gate of roses.
Pip: Goodbye, garden! Your flowers made the whole day bright.
Bella: Helping a lost baby is the best adventure of all.
Bella: The garden gate closes softly behind us — what a day!
Bella: Tomorrow I will chase the rainbow balloon over the hills — will you come with me?
scripts.title: Bella and the Butterfly Garden

scripts.hint: Rusty's tow hook saves the day when the parade's biggest float breaks down.
lines: Rusty: Why is the whole town hanging flags across the street?
Rusty: Today is the Great Toy Parade, and I lead the way!
Rusty: Sam, polish my tow hook — it must shine in the parade!
Sam: The drums are beating already, Rusty — listen to that boom boom!
Rusty: I roll out of the workshop yard onto the flag-lined street.
Sam: Look, Rusty! The toy soldiers are marching behind us!
Rusty: We pass the market square where everyone waves and cheers.
Rusty: The big flower float follows us, smelling of jasmine.
Sam: The parade is turning onto the old stone bridge now!
Rusty: Oh no! The flower float stopped — its wheel has come off!
Rusty: The whole parade is stuck behind it on the bridge!
Sam: Wait, Rusty... your tow hook is exactly what a float needs!
Rusty: Stand back, friends — Rusty the tow truck is on the job!
Rusty: I hook the float gently and pull with all my strength.
Sam: The float is moving again — slow and steady over the bridge!
Rusty: We roll into the park avenue while the band plays louder.
Sam: The mayor is waving from the park gate, Rusty!
Rusty: I park the float under the big banyan tree for repairs.
Sam: The toy mechanic fixes the wheel with a happy hammer song.
Rusty: The parade circles the park one last joyful time.
Rusty: Confetti rains on my roof like colourful snow.
Sam: You are the hero of the parade, Rusty — hooray!
Rusty: A tow hook is small, but it can carry a whole parade.
Rusty: I drive home under the flags as the sun goes down.
Rusty: Tomorrow I will visit the harbour where the pirate ship sleeps — will you come with me?
scripts.title: Rusty and the Great Toy Parade

scripts.hint: Bruno the big blue truck rides a ferry to an island and meets a gentle giant of the sea.
lines: Bruno: Why is that road ending right at the edge of the sea?
Bruno: Today I ride the big ferry to Banana Island!
Bruno: Nina, check my parcels — every box must reach the island.
Nina: The ferry horn is calling us, Bruno — toot toooot!
Bruno: I roll down the harbour ramp and onto the ferry deck.
Nina: The ferry is rocking softly as we leave the harbour.
Bruno: Seagulls fly beside us, racing the white ferry foam.
Bruno: I can see the island growing bigger — green hills and palms!
Nina: Look, Bruno! Something huge is swimming beside the ferry!
Bruno: Oh no! Is it a sea monster coming to bump our boat?
Bruno: It sprays a fountain of water high into the air!
Nina: Wait, Bruno... it is not a monster — it is a friendly whale!
Bruno: The whale sings a deep song that hums through the deck.
Nina: She is guiding the ferry around the shallow rocks!
Bruno: The captain waves his hat — thank you, gentle whale!
Bruno: We reach the island dock safe and sound, hooray!
Nina: The island children are waiting for their parcels, Bruno!
Bruno: I drive up the island road through the banana grove.
Bruno: Every parcel delivered — books, toys and a birthday cake!
Nina: The whale spouts one last goodbye fountain at the dock.
Bruno: I ride the evening ferry home under a pink sky.
Bruno: The harbour lights twinkle as we roll off the deck.
Nina: What a giant adventure for one delivery day!
Bruno: Big trucks can be gentle, and big whales can be friends.
Bruno: Tomorrow I will race the night train to the mountains — will you come with me?
scripts.title: Bruno and the Island Ferry

scripts.hint: Milo climbs the windy hill for the kite festival and rescues a runaway kite.
lines: Milo: Why is the sky above the hill full of dancing diamonds?
Milo: Today I climb Windy Hill for the big kite festival!
Milo: Coco, hold our little kite tight — the wind is playful!
Coco: The park path is already busy with kite families, Milo!
Milo: I drive up the winding hill road, past the ice-cream cart.
Coco: Look, Milo! A red kite is doing loops over the pine grove!
Milo: We cross the stream bridge where the water sparkles below.
Milo: The hilltop meadow is a sea of colour and laughter.
Coco: Our kite is dancing — up, up, up into the blue!
Milo: Oh no! A gust tore a little girl's kite from her hands!
Milo: The kite is flying away over the pine trees!
Coco: Wait, Milo... the kite string is tangled on the old windmill!
Milo: I will drive to the windmill — follow me, little friend!
Milo: The windmill keeper climbs up and frees the kite string.
Coco: The kite floats down slowly, right onto your roof, Milo!
Milo: We drive it back across the meadow to the little girl.
Coco: She is hugging her kite — what a happy smile!
Milo: Now all the kites fly together like a rainbow flock.
Milo: The sun paints the hilltop gold as the festival ends.
Coco: Our kite gets a tiny prize ribbon for the bravest flight!
Milo: We roll down the hill road under the first evening stars.
Milo: The wind whispers goodnight through the pine grove.
Coco: Goodbye, Windy Hill! We will fly with you again.
Milo: Small cars can do big rescues on windy days.
Milo: Tomorrow I will deliver the snow letters to the hilltop house — will you come with me?
scripts.title: Milo and the Kite Festival

scripts.hint: Leo the green jeep explores the jungle and helps a baby elephant find its herd.
lines: Leo: What was that giant ROAR shaking the jungle leaves?
Leo: Today I explore the deep green jungle — safari time!
Leo: Zara, sit tall on my spare wheel — adventure ahead!
Zara: The bamboo road is cool and shady, Leo!
Leo: I splash through the shallow river crossing, drip drip.
Leo: A waterfall pours like a silver curtain beside the track.
Zara: Look, Leo! Monkeys are swinging above the banana clearing!
Leo: I climb the lookout rock for a view over the whole jungle.
Zara: The jungle spreads below us like a green ocean!
Leo: Oh no! I hear a tiny trumpet crying behind the ferns!
Leo: Something big is pushing through the bushes towards us!
Zara: Wait, Leo... it is only a baby elephant, lost and muddy!
Leo: Do not cry, little one — we will find your family together.
Leo: The baby follows my jeep tracks along the river track.
Zara: Listen! Answering trumpets are calling from the clearing!
Leo: There they are — the whole herd waiting by the waterhole!
Zara: The mother elephant sprays a happy shower over everyone!
Leo: I get a cool jungle shower too — what a thank-you!
Leo: We watch the herd drink as the sun turns golden.
Zara: Goodbye, jungle friends! Stay wild and happy.
Leo: I drive out through the bamboo gate under the stars.
Leo: The fireflies light my muddy wheels all the way home.
Zara: That roar at the start was just the jungle saying hello!
Leo: A brave jeep is never scared of a friendly jungle.
Leo: Tomorrow I will race the rafts down the great river — will you come with me?
scripts.title: Leo and the Jungle Safari

scripts.hint: Rayo helps harvest apples and discovers why the scarecrow keeps moving.
lines: Rayo: Why are a thousand red apples shining on that hill?
Rayo: Today is harvest day at the apple orchard!
Rayo: Teddy, bring the baskets — we have work to do!
Teddy: The orchard gate is made of twisted apple branches, Rayo!
Rayo: I drive between the apple rows, apples bowing above me.
Teddy: The farmer is picking the ripest, reddest apples!
Rayo: I carry full baskets down to the farmhouse yard.
Rayo: The old cider mill is turning with a happy creak-creak.
Teddy: Look, Rayo! The scarecrow in the hay field waved at me!
Rayo: Oh no! Scarecrows do not wave — something is hiding there!
Rayo: The scarecrow's hat keeps bobbing up and down by itself!
Teddy: Wait, Rayo... a little goat is standing under the scarecrow!
Rayo: The goat is bumping the pole to shake apples down!
Teddy: Clever goat! She catches the apples before they bruise!
Rayo: We load the goat's apples into my baskets too.
Rayo: Down the hill road we roll, baskets full and shining.
Teddy: The farmer presses sweet juice for the whole village!
Rayo: Everyone drinks apple juice under the orchard trees.
Teddy: The goat gets a whole basket of apples as her prize!
Rayo: The sun sets red as an apple over the hay field.
Rayo: I drive home with one apple tied to my mirror.
Teddy: Goodbye, orchard! Your apples are the sweetest treasure.
Rayo: Harvest day is the happiest day of the autumn.
Rayo: A fast car and full baskets — what a perfect team!
Rayo: Tomorrow I will explore the old castle on the cliff — will you come with me?
scripts.title: Rayo and the Apple Orchard

scripts.hint: Bella's bright yellow roof becomes the guide that brings a drifting balloon safely down.
lines: Bella: What is that giant rainbow floating over the meadow?
Bella: Today a hot-air balloon is visiting our valley!
Bella: Pip, the fairground meadow is full of flags and music!
Pip: The balloon is striped like a rainbow lollipop, Bella!
Bella: I park by the river bank to watch it rise.
Bella: Up it goes, over the village rooftops and chimneys!
Pip: Look, Bella! The balloon is drifting towards Windmill Hill!
Bella: The wind is pushing it faster and faster — oh dear!
Pip: The balloon basket is waving a big white flag at us!
Bella: Oh no! The balloon cannot find a safe place to land!
Bella: The lakeside field is too wet and the hill is too rocky!
Pip: Wait, Bella... the pilot is pointing at YOU, Bella!
Bella: Of course! My bright yellow roof is easy to see from the sky!
Bella: I will drive to the big flat meadow — follow me, balloon!
Pip: The balloon is turning — it is following your yellow roof!
Bella: I circle the meadow slowly so the pilot can aim for me.
Pip: Down, down, down — the basket is almost touching the grass!
Bella: The balloon lands softly right beside my wheels. Hooray!
Pip: The pilot gives us a ride in the basket — up we float!
Bella: From up here, our whole valley looks like a tiny toy town!
Bella: We float down gently as the evening light turns pink.
Pip: Goodbye, rainbow balloon! What a sky-high adventure.
Bella: Being bright and helpful can save the whole day.
Bella: I drive home along the lakeside under the first stars.
Bella: Tomorrow I will follow the honey bees to their meadow — will you come with me?
scripts.title: Bella and the Rainbow Balloon

scripts.hint: Milo delivers winter letters through the snow with help from a friendly sled dog.
lines: Milo: Why is the whole village wrapped in a white blanket?
Milo: Today I deliver the winter post through the snow!
Milo: Coco, the post office gave me a sack of letters and parcels!
Coco: The village street is quiet and sparkly this morning, Milo!
Milo: I cross the icy bridge very, very slowly — no sliding!
Milo: The pine forest road is lined with snowy Christmas trees.
Coco: Look, Milo! Smoke curls from the farm lane cottages!
Milo: First delivery — a birthday parcel for the farmer's twins!
Coco: The twins wave from the window with hot chocolate mugs!
Milo: Oh no! The hilltop road is too snowy — my wheels just spin!
Milo: The last letter must reach the hilltop house before dark!
Coco: Wait, Milo... something is racing down the hill towards us!
Milo: It is Bruno the sled dog, pulling an empty red sled!
Coco: We can load the letter sack onto his sled, Milo!
Milo: Bruno barks twice and dashes up the hill path like the wind.
Milo: I follow his paw prints slowly, cheering him on.
Coco: The hilltop grandmother opens her letter and smiles wide!
Milo: She gives Bruno a biscuit and me a shiny snowflake badge.
Coco: We slide back down to the village as the lamps turn on.
Milo: Every letter is delivered — the post run is complete!
Milo: The post office master rings the big brass bell for us.
Coco: Goodnight, snowy village! Sleep warm and cosy.
Milo: When wheels cannot go, good friends carry the day.
Milo: Steam rises from my engine in the cold evening air.
Milo: Tomorrow I will race through the great garden maze — will you come with me?
scripts.title: Milo and the Snowy Post Run

scripts.hint: Bruno must reach the station before the night train leaves — or the mountain village gets no mail.
lines: Bruno: Why is the depot master running towards me with a red flag?
Bruno: Tonight I carry the mountain village's mail to the station!
Bruno: Nina, the night train leaves at moonrise — we must hurry!
Nina: Your headlights are two bright moons on the depot road, Bruno!
Bruno: I roll past the sleeping level crossing, quiet as a mouse.
Bruno: The tunnel road echoes my engine like a friendly drum.
Nina: Look, Bruno! The station platform lights are already glowing!
Bruno: Wait — that is the wrong glow. The moon is not up yet!
Nina: The real station is still two hills away, Bruno!
Bruno: Oh no! A fallen tree blocks the mountain pass road!
Bruno: The train will leave without the mail — think, Bruno, think!
Nina: Wait, Bruno... I can hear the river road below the pass!
Bruno: The old riverside road! It is longer, but it is clear!
Bruno: I turn down the valley road, engine singing bravely.
Nina: The river shines silver beside us in the moonlight!
Bruno: We climb the last hill — the station clock is in sight!
Nina: The train driver is waving — he waited one extra minute!
Bruno: I brake beside the mail wagon just as the whistle blows!
Bruno: Every mail sack loaded — the mountain village will get its letters!
Nina: The train rolls away into the night, windows glowing gold.
Bruno: The station master gives us hot soup and a big thank-you.
Bruno: I drive home slowly under a sky full of sleepy stars.
Nina: Goodnight, night train! We will race you again soon.
Bruno: Big and slow can still win the race that matters.
Bruno: Tomorrow I will sail to the island of bananas again — will you come with me?
scripts.title: Bruno and the Night Train Race

scripts.hint: Leo joins the great raft race and shares his raft with a very slow racer.
lines: Leo: Why is everyone carrying wooden rafts down to the river?
Leo: Today is the Great River Raft Race — and I am racing!
Leo: Zara, our raft is the greenest raft on the whole river!
Zara: The raft dock is crowded with laughing racers, Leo!
Leo: The starting horn blows — splash! Off we float!
Leo: We drift past the reed maze where dragonflies zoom.
Zara: Look, Leo! The waterfall bend is coming up fast!
Leo: Hold tight — whoosh! Down the gentle waterfall slide!
Zara: We are in third place, Leo — paddle, paddle, paddle!
Leo: Oh no! A tiny turtle is swimming all alone behind us!
Leo: The poor turtle can never win at this slow speed!
Zara: Wait, Leo... winning is not the only way to have fun!
Leo: Hop on our raft, little turtle — racers help racers!
Leo: With the turtle aboard, we float slower but happier.
Zara: The sandy beach checkpoint is cheering for the turtle!
Leo: Other racers slow down too and join our friendly flotilla.
Zara: Now it is a parade of rafts, not a race at all!
Leo: We cross under the finish bridge together, all at once.
Zara: The judges give the turtle the Golden Friendship Cup!
Leo: We share a picnic on the sandy beach as the sun sets.
Leo: The river rocks our empty raft like a sleepy boat.
Zara: Goodbye, river! Today everyone was a winner.
Leo: A race where everyone finishes together is the best race.
Leo: I drive home along the riverbank under the moon.
Leo: Tomorrow I will solve the mystery of the moving castle ghost — will you come with me?
scripts.title: Leo and the River Raft Race

scripts.hint: Rayo visits the old castle fair and finds out what the 'ghost' in the tower really is.
lines: Rayo: Who keeps flashing a white light from the castle tower?
Rayo: Today the old castle is holding a fair on the cliff!
Rayo: Teddy, the castle gate is opening its giant wooden doors!
Teddy: The courtyard is full of fair stalls and music, Rayo!
Rayo: I drive over the moat bridge, flags snapping above me.
Teddy: Look, Rayo! Jugglers are tossing rainbow balls by the tower!
Rayo: I wind up the tower road, round and round the stone walls.
Rayo: The garden maze below looks like a green puzzle.
Teddy: The white light flashed again from the very top window!
Rayo: Oh no! Everyone says a ghost lives in the tower room!
Rayo: The tower stairs are dark — but I am a brave race car!
Teddy: Wait, Rayo... I can hear a soft hoot-hoot from the window!
Rayo: It is not a ghost at all — it is a great white owl!
Teddy: The owl's white wings flash in the sun when she flies!
Rayo: The owl has a nest of fluffy babies in the tower room!
Teddy: The fair crowd cheers — the castle ghost is a mother owl!
Rayo: The castle keeper names the owl Queen of the Fair.
Rayo: We feast on the banquet lawn as the fiddles play.
Teddy: The owl soars over the fair one last time at sunset.
Rayo: I drive down the cliff road as the castle lamps glow.
Rayo: The moat reflects the fireworks like a second sky.
Teddy: Goodbye, old castle! Your secret is safe with us.
Rayo: Scary stories often hide a gentle surprise.
Rayo: Every fair is better with a mystery to solve.
Rayo: Tomorrow I will help the bees in the honey meadow — will you come with me?
scripts.title: Rayo and the Castle Fair

scripts.hint: A whole swarm of bees follows Bella because she is yellow like a flower — she must lead them home.
lines: Bella: Why is a buzzing golden cloud following my roof?
Bella: Today I visit the honey bee meadow on the hill!
Bella: Pip, the clover field is humming with a thousand bees!
Pip: The hive trees stand in a row like little bee hotels, Bella!
Bella: I roll down the stream path where the water runs sweet.
Bella: The farmer's barn is painted with sunflowers and bees.
Pip: Look, Bella! The bees are landing all over your yellow roof!
Bella: They think I am the biggest flower in the whole meadow!
Pip: More and more bees are joining — it is a whole swarm now!
Bella: Oh no! The swarm's hive blew down in last night's storm!
Bella: The bees have no home — that is why they follow me!
Pip: Wait, Bella... the farmer built a brand-new hive by the barn!
Bella: Bees, follow my yellow roof — I will take you home!
Bella: I drive very slowly down the sunflower lane, buzz buzz.
Pip: The swarm is streaming behind you like a golden river!
Bella: We reach the new hive — in you go, little bees!
Pip: The queen bee is first, and all her bees follow her in!
Bella: The farmer thanks us with a jar of golden honey.
Pip: We taste one drop — sunshine in a spoon!
Bella: The meadow hums a happy evening song around us.
Bella: I drive home past the hive trees under a honey sky.
Pip: Goodbye, bees! We will taste your honey again soon.
Bella: Being the colour of sunshine is a superpower after all.
Bella: Every small friend deserves a safe home.
Bella: Tomorrow I will fly with the rainbow balloon again — will you come with me?
scripts.title: Bella and the Honey Bee Meadow

scripts.hint: Rusty helps raise a sunken old ship at the harbour — and its treasure surprises everyone.
lines: Rusty: What is that crooked mast sticking out of the harbour water?
Rusty: Today the harbour divers found a sunken old ship!
Rusty: Sam, the pier is full of ropes, boats and busy sailors!
Sam: The old ship sleeps on the harbour bottom, Rusty!
Rusty: I park at the boatyard where the crane boat is waiting.
Sam: Look, Rusty! The divers are tying giant balloons to the ship!
Rusty: When the balloons fill with air, the ship will float up!
Rusty: My job is to pull the ship to the dock with my tow cable.
Sam: The balloons are rising — the mast is moving, Rusty!
Rusty: Oh no! One rope snapped — the ship is tipping sideways!
Rusty: If she tips too far, she will sink all over again!
Sam: Wait, Rusty... your spare tow cable can hold that side!
Rusty: Quick, Sam — hook my cable to the harbour bollard!
Rusty: I pull with all my might — the ship steadies, slow and grand.
Sam: She is rising! The old ship is floating again, hooray!
Rusty: We tow her gently to the sunset dock, drip by drip.
Sam: The captain opens the old treasure chest from the hold!
Rusty: It is not gold — it is full of old wooden toys!
Sam: The toys belonged to sailors' children, long long ago!
Rusty: The harbour children share the toys on the pier.
Rusty: The old ship will become a floating toy museum.
Sam: Goodbye, old ship! Your treasure made everyone smile.
Rusty: The best treasure is the kind you can share.
Rusty: I coil my tow cable under the harbour lights.
Rusty: Tomorrow I will lead an even bigger parade through town — will you come with me?
scripts.title: Rusty and the Sunken Pirate Ship

scripts.hint: Milo races through a giant hedge maze and finds a tiny guide at its heart.
lines: Milo: Why do these garden hedges stand taller than the houses?
Milo: Today I race the Great Garden Maze from gate to centre!
Milo: Coco, the maze gate is covered in climbing roses!
Coco: The hedge paths smell of rain and green leaves, Milo!
Milo: First turn — left! The path curls like a snail shell.
Coco: Look, Milo! A topiary elephant is hiding in this corner!
Milo: Second turn — right! A topiary giraffe watches us pass.
Milo: The rose tunnel arches over us, pink and sweet.
Coco: We can hear the fountain — the centre must be close!
Milo: Oh no! Every path looks the same — we are going in circles!
Milo: The topiary elephant again — we passed it three times!
Coco: Wait, Milo... a tiny mouse is waving at us from the hedge!
Milo: The little mouse knows the maze — she visits every day!
Coco: She runs ahead — follow the mouse, Milo, follow her!
Milo: Left, right, under the arch — the mouse never hesitates!
Coco: The fountain! We reached the centre of the maze!
Milo: In the centre stands a golden sundial older than the garden.
Coco: The mouse gets a feast of seeds as her guide's prize!
Milo: We drive out slowly, following our own tyre tracks.
Milo: The picnic hill overlooks the whole green puzzle.
Coco: From up here the maze looks like a giant green ribbon!
Milo: We picnic as the garden lamps come on one by one.
Coco: Goodbye, garden maze! We solved you together.
Milo: The smallest guide can lead the biggest adventure.
Milo: Tomorrow I will fly our kite on Windy Hill again — will you come with me?
scripts.title: Milo and the Great Garden Maze
